title: How can we simplify a division of two powers?
description: Ten to the power four is divided by five to the power four by pairing each ten with one five, and the answer is written as one power. Working out both powers checks the answer. Keeko's doubt is that dividing the bases and the exponents gives only one two.
teaching_notes: One idea: powers with the same exponent are divided by pairing the bases, so the bases are divided and the exponent stays. Watch for students who divide the exponents as well and stop at one pair.

source: Simplify 10⁴ ÷ 5⁴ and write it in exponential form. Check by
video_script.why: The child can pair the bases when multiplying powers that share an exponent and now does the same when dividing them.
video_script.substitution: The book's own ten to the power four divided by five to the power four, written in full and checked by working out both powers.
video_script.anchor: four tens above four fives on the board, each ten paired with one five
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks ten divided by five is two and four divided by four is one, so the answer is two. There are four pairs of ten and five, and each pair gives its own two, so the four twos are multiplied.
video_script.payoff_line: Ten to the power four divided by five to the power four is two to the power four

final_answer.spoken: two to the power four, which is sixteen

maths_rules: slip: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 and 4 ÷ 4 = 1 gives 2, which is wrong
video_script.design: One idea: pair each base and keep the exponent. The four pairs stay on the board all video; the one power and the value 16 are left open until the answer; one slip at the end.

beats.on_screen: title card, From your book; 10⁴ ÷ 5⁴ on the board

marks.book: the title card From your book arrives
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about dividing powers.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>Ten to the power four is divided by five to the power four.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we simplify it and write it as one power?
And how can we check it by working out both powers?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Ten to the power four means four tens multiplied.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Five to the power four means four fives multiplied.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, ten to the power four divided by five to the power four.

beats.on_screen: To find: 10⁴ ÷ 5⁴ as one power; check by working out both powers
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write it as one power.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Then we check by working out both powers.

marks.one: both powers are written in full
marks.tens: the four tens are lined up over the four fives

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, write both powers in full.
<bookmark mark='tens'/>Four tens multiplied are divided by four fives multiplied.

marks.two: each 10 is paired with one 5 in four pairs
marks.open: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 is written with the one power left open

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, pair each ten with one five.
<bookmark mark='pair'/>Each pair is ten divided by five, which is two.
There are four pairs, so four twos are multiplied.
<bookmark mark='open'/>Writing that as one power is left to find.

marks.div: 10000 ÷ 625 is written with the result left open

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, check by working out both powers.
Ten to the power four is ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Five to the power four is six hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Ten thousand divided by six hundred twenty five is left to find.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>Ten to the power four divided by five to the power four is two to the power four.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Ten thousand divided by six hundred twenty five is sixteen.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>Two to the power four is also sixteen, so the check agrees.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the four pairs
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 and 4 ÷ 4 = 1 appear with the answer 2, then are crossed out; the four pairs each show 2

marks.count: the answer 2 is crossed out and the four pairs are lit up, each showing 2
marks.fix: × signs are written between the four twos

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks ten divided by five is two.
Four divided by four is one, so the answer is two.
<bookmark mark='count'/>But there are four pairs, and each pair gives its own two.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The four twos are multiplied, so we cannot stop at one two.
